correctness.rationale: For trees n>=3, every leaf has leaf-degree zero, total leaf-neighbor weight is L_n, and the leaf count increments by one exactly when a nonleaf is selected. Hence P(delta L=1 | L_n)=1-a L_n/(a n+L_n). The unique drift fixed point r in (1/2,1), exact deviation recursion with contraction b_n=a^2/[(a+L_n/n)(a+r)], and L2/L4 estimates justify replacing it in L2 by linear contraction kappa=a²/(a+r)². Bounded-increment triangular martingale CLT yields V=r(1-r)/(1+2kappa) and moment convergence; derivative of V as function of r gives unique maximizing root of 6r³-15r²+16r-6 and threshold crossing 1/12. Independent rational finite-chain mass conservation, fixed-point algebra, and symbolic derivative checks passed. Finite enumeration does not prove the asymptotic normal law.
residual_risks: The L4 contraction and asymptotic variance arguments are analytical and do not quantify finite-n convergence rates.
Fixed a>0 only, excluding simultaneous a,n limits.
